meta.title: Chess learning curriculum — staged plan, pearls, metrics

evidence_grades.A: Replicated controlled experiment (often cognitive science / motor learning, extrapolated to chess)
evidence_grades.B: Large observational chess dataset, no randomisation
evidence_grades.D: Single anecdote, self-report, or historical stereotype

notes: No chess training method has a randomised controlled trial behind it; grade all content accordingly.
Stage progression is gated by exit_criteria measured in the learner's own reviewed games, not by rating alone.

schedule_constraints.shift_days: 12h day shifts; evenings are low-yield for new-pattern encoding
schedule_constraints.off_day_mornings: highest-yield slot for long games and new material
schedule_constraints.rule: No new material or long games after a shift; easy repetition only

learner_profile_defaults.realistic_outcome: 1600–1800 in 2–3 years at 5–7 hr/week is a good outcome; 2000 is an outlier for adult starters.

standing_orders.text: Every game gets a written post-mortem or it didn't count. Narrative first, then engine.
Engine's job is narrow: which move lost material / where eval swung ≥1.5. No deeper lines until Stage 3.
Time control slow enough to run your checklist: 15+10 minimum through Stage 2. Blitz is not training until Stage 3. Bullet is never training.
Fix the recurring error until it stops recurring. One error type per week.
Puzzles: mixed themes, slow, written full line, missing line = wrong.
Openings = ideas to move 8–10. No memorised lines until Stage 3.
No new material after a shift. Shift evenings: 15 min easy tactics or a rewatched lesson.
Never ask a chat LLM to read a position directly; ask it to explain engine output.
Chess960 once a month as a diagnostic of internalised principles, not as a training diet.
Don't copy a GM's childhood. Use elite methods only at the stage tagged for them.

stages.name: Floor: move safety

giants_to_copy.name: Morphy
giants_to_copy.lesson: Develop every piece, castle, open a central file before attacking; count tempi in open positions

giants_to_copy.name: Steinitz
giants_to_copy.lesson: Don't attack without a reason; keep the position closed if behind in development

giants_to_copy.name: Capablanca
giants_to_copy.lesson: When ahead, trade pieces and play the endgame

giants_to_copy.name: Botvinnik (method only)
giants_to_copy.lesson: Annotate every loss: find the move that hung material

stages.mechanism: Games are decided by one-move material losses; opponents leave kings central and pieces undefended. You cannot yet verify compensation.

weekly_blocks.name: Long game + review
weekly_blocks.content: Play; write narrative (first material loss / what was threatened the move before / did I run the check); engine Game Review for that one question only

weekly_blocks.name: Lesson
weekly_blocks.content: Bartholomew Chess Fundamentals; Chessbrah Building Habits rules

weekly_blocks.name: Easy tactics
weekly_blocks.content: Easy, mixed themes, slow, full line stated before moving

weekly_blocks.name: Endgame drill
weekly_blocks.content: K+Q and K+R mates; K+P vs K opposition; vs engine until automatic

micro_steps.task: Set up account. Play 3 games at 15+10. After each, write 3 lines: first material loss / what was threatened the move before / did I check. Nothing else.
Add the per-move mantra: his checks, captures, threats after my move. Time it. Target habitual by week 4.
Add 'count before you capture': attackers vs defenders; what remains after the full sequence.
K+Q and K+R mate drills to <30 s. First Chess960 game as a test of development principles.
K+P vs K (opposition). Begin tagging each review with one error type.
Pick most frequent error tag; it is the week's only study target.
Introduce 'when ahead, trade pieces'. Review for compliance.
Audit against exit criteria. If unmet, repeat weeks 5–8. Do not advance.

resources: Heisman — A Guide to Chess Improvement

stages.name: Principles under pressure

giants_to_copy.name: Morphy / Steinitz
giants_to_copy.lesson: Continued

giants_to_copy.name: Lasker
giants_to_copy.lesson: In equal positions, pick the move that gives the opponent the most ways to go wrong

giants_to_copy.name: Capablanca
giants_to_copy.lesson: Every opening move serves a middlegame plan

stages.mechanism: Safety habit exists; now make it hold under clock pressure and add a one-sentence plan per opening.

exit_criteria.note: One opening per colour, plan to move 8–10 in one sentence

weekly_blocks.name: Long game + review
weekly_blocks.content: As S0; add 'what does he want next?' as third question

weekly_blocks.name: Lesson
weekly_blocks.content: Naroditsky speedruns at your band; Heisman real-chess thought process

micro_steps.task: Choose 1.e4 or 1.d4 and one reply to each as Black; learn the plan, not the line; stop deliberating.
Start a one-page recurring-errors sheet; retire an entry only after 10 clean games.

resources: Heisman — A Guide to Chess Improvement

stages.name: Club: structure, endgames, honest annotation

giants_to_copy.name: Capablanca
giants_to_copy.lesson: Planning from the opening; endgame technique; Chernev's move-by-move games

giants_to_copy.name: Tarrasch
giants_to_copy.lesson: Mobility rules as defaults: rooks behind passed pawns, don't block your own bishops

giants_to_copy.name: Botvinnik
giants_to_copy.lesson: Narrow repertoire studied as typical positions; annotations exposed to someone stronger

giants_to_copy.name: Steinitz
giants_to_copy.lesson: Weak pawns matter more as pieces come off; count pawn islands before trading

giants_to_copy.name: Lasker
giants_to_copy.lesson: Practical choice in equal positions

stages.mechanism: Opponents leave theory by move 8; middlegame plan and endings decide. Rules are training wheels until pattern recognition replaces them.

weekly_blocks.name: Long games
weekly_blocks.content: Kraai method: narrative first, test against moves on a board, engine last

weekly_blocks.name: Easy tactics, mass repetition
weekly_blocks.content: Aagaard: basic simple tactics, every line written, missing answer = wrong; mixed themes

weekly_blocks.name: Study block
weekly_blocks.content: Rotate: Silman endgame band / Chernev Logical Chess / one annotated Capablanca game

weekly_blocks.name: Opening repair
weekly_blocks.content: Only for review-identified recurring problems; explorer: where does my line end, what's the middlegame?

micro_steps.task: Build the ~20-endgame list (Soltis/Heisman via Silman); drill one per week vs engine.
Set a standing monthly review with a stronger player (club, Dojo cohort, or paid hour).
Apply 'what if I play the second move first?' to every candidate sequence.

resources: Chernev — Logical Chess: Move by Move
Silman — Complete Endgame Course (to your band only)
Kraai — How to analyze your own games

stages.name: Strong club: calculation discipline and positional vocabulary

giants_to_copy.name: Nimzowitsch / Petrosian
giants_to_copy.lesson: Prophylaxis as habit; blockade with knights; positional exchange sac when files are closed

giants_to_copy.name: Alekhine
giants_to_copy.lesson: Steer into positions with live options while keeping structure sound

giants_to_copy.name: Karpov
giants_to_copy.lesson: Remove counterplay first, then press

giants_to_copy.name: Fischer
giants_to_copy.lesson: Bishop-vs-knight judgment

giants_to_copy.name: Carlsen (mindset)
giants_to_copy.lesson: Mistakes are a consequence of tension; play on in equal positions; test 'theoretical draws'

giants_to_copy.name: Kotov
giants_to_copy.lesson: Candidate moves written out

giants_to_ignore: AlphaZero h-pawn marches / early pawn sacs as defaults
stages.mechanism: Static compensation is now evaluable; dynamic long-term compensation still exceeds calculation. Written lines expose visualisation failures.

weekly_blocks.name: Positional study
weekly_blocks.content: Silman Reassess Your Chess; Nimzowitsch My System Part 2+

weekly_blocks.name: Prophylaxis exercise
weekly_blocks.content: Dvoretsky-style: find the opponent's best move, then prevent it

micro_steps.task: Adopt Aagaard's three questions on every critical position; show evidence in annotations.
Force a written second candidate before committing (Einstellung countermeasure).
Optional Woodpecker cycle as commitment device; mechanism unproven.

resources: Silman — How to Reassess Your Chess

stages.name: Expert+

giants_to_copy.name: Dvoretsky
giants_to_copy.lesson: Set positions played both colours vs a stronger player; written solutions to hard studies; exhaustive own-game analysis

giants_to_copy.name: Kasparov
giants_to_copy.lesson: Record novelties; engine-check afterwards for sobering

giants_to_copy.name: AlphaZero (with understanding)
giants_to_copy.lesson: King mobility; rook-pawn pushes vs castled king only with stable centre; redeploy before being kicked

giants_to_copy.name: Sindarov 2026
giants_to_copy.lesson: Recognise more, calculate less; win on the clock

stages.mechanism: Ceiling work pays only now; coach-driven plan expected.

micro_steps.task: Get a coach; make the plan yours.

pearls.text: Hope chess is a hung piece with a story attached.
pearls.mechanism: Moving without checking the opponent's forcing replies.
pearls.action: After choosing a move: his checks, captures, threats — before releasing it.

pearls.text: Count before you capture.
pearls.mechanism: Material outcome depends on the whole exchange sequence, not the first capture.
pearls.action: Attackers vs defenders on the square; what remains after the sequence.

pearls.text: Your first blunder is the game.
pearls.mechanism: Under-1400: first ≥2-pawn blunder before move 17; over-1900: ~move 40.
pearls.action: Track move-of-first-blunder as your primary metric.

pearls.text: Undefended pieces are pending results — check them every move.
pearls.mechanism: Loose pieces are the most common target at low levels.
pearls.action: Scan both sides for undefended pieces each move.

pearls.text: An uncastled king is the chief complaint. Nothing elective until it's addressed.
pearls.mechanism: Central king + open lines = Morphy's attacking preconditions.
pearls.action: Castle by move 10 unless there is a concrete reason not to.

pearls.text: Develop everything, then attack. Morphy didn't sacrifice until every piece was in.
pearls.mechanism: Attacks fail without superior force at the point of contact.
pearls.action: No attack until all minor pieces are developed and the king is safe.

pearls.text: Don't attack without a reason. If you can't name his error, you haven't earned the attack.
pearls.mechanism: Against correct defence an attack fails and the attacker ends up worse.
pearls.action: Name the concrete advantage before committing to an attack.

pearls.text: A pawn down with 'activity' is a pawn down.
pearls.mechanism: You cannot yet verify compensation.
pearls.action: Decline speculative sacrifices until Stage 3.

pearls.text: Ahead? Trade pieces, not pawns. Behind? Keep pieces on.
pearls.mechanism: Simplification converts material; complexity creates swindle chances.
pearls.action: Check material balance before every trade offer.

pearls.text: A long think is a symptom of non-recognition, and it predicts a blunder.
pearls.mechanism: Longer think time correlates positively with blundering; it signals the position isn't in your library.
pearls.action: Staring >3 min → take the safest move and bank the clock.

pearls.text: Slow enough to run the checklist, or the time control is the diagnosis.
pearls.mechanism: Safety habits need time to execute until automatic.
pearls.action: 15+10 minimum through Stage 2.

pearls.text: Blitz is a stress test, not a treatment. Bullet is television.
pearls.mechanism: Blitz reveals weaknesses but a beginner has no blunder-check reflex to lean on.
pearls.action: No blitz as training until Stage 3; bullet never.
pearls.source: Dojo / Heisman / Kraai (contested by Dlugy, Polgár, Naroditsky for stronger players)

pearls.text: Review beats play ~5:1 per hour. A game without a post-mortem is a game you paid for and didn't get.
pearls.mechanism: Game review 4.41 vs games 0.86 rating pts/hr (observational, n=44k).
pearls.action: 100% of long games reviewed.

pearls.text: Write the narrative before the engine.
pearls.mechanism: Error-location quality, not repetition count, predicts next-day performance.
pearls.action: Narrative → test against moves → engine last.

pearls.text: At this level the engine answers one question: which move lost material. Close it after that.
pearls.mechanism: Deeper lines are noise until you can evaluate them.
pearls.action: Game Review for the blunder only.

pearls.text: Don't ask a chatbot to read a board. Ask it to explain what Stockfish said.
pearls.mechanism: LLMs hallucinate pieces and checks on direct PGN; work as translators over engine output.
pearls.action: LLM only downstream of engine/Maia output.

pearls.text: No new patterns after a 12-hour shift.
pearls.mechanism: One night of sleep deprivation cuts new-memory encoding ~40%.
pearls.action: Shift evenings = easy repetition only.

pearls.text: Morning brain plays slower and better. Long games live in off-day mornings.
pearls.mechanism: Fast-chess decisions get faster and less accurate through the day across chronotypes.
pearls.action: Schedule long games in off-day mornings.

pearls.text: Openings: ideas, not lines.
pearls.mechanism: Opponents leave theory by move 8; mistakes happen in middlegame/endgame.
pearls.action: One-sentence plan per opening; no memorised lines until Stage 3.

pearls.text: Plateau ≠ ceiling.
pearls.mechanism: Rating follows a power law in games played; asymptote ~750–1,000 rated games.
pearls.action: Judge by error metrics, not rating, until ~750 rated games.

pearls.text: Themed puzzle sets feel good and teach worse. Mix the themes.
pearls.mechanism: Blocked practice: faster in-session gains, worse retention, overconfidence.
pearls.action: Random/mixed puzzle sets.

pearls.text: Easy tactics, mass repetition, every line written, a missing line counts as wrong.
pearls.mechanism: Floor skills need automaticity, not difficulty.
pearls.action: Daily 15–20 min easy tactics, written.

pearls.text: About 20 endgames carry you to 2000. Learn them cold and stop.
pearls.mechanism: Under-2000 games rarely need more; time is better spent elsewhere.
pearls.action: Build and drill the 20-endgame list; stop there.

pearls.text: What if I play the second move first?
pearls.mechanism: Move-order errors are the commonest calculation failure.
pearls.action: Move-order check on every sequence.

pearls.text: In equal positions, choose the move that gives him the most ways to go wrong.
pearls.mechanism: Nettlesomeness: inducing opponent errors even without the engine's first choice.
pearls.action: Prefer problem-posing moves over 'correct but easy' ones.

pearls.text: Weak pawns get weaker as pieces come off. Count pawn islands before you trade.
pearls.mechanism: Isolated/backward/doubled pawns become permanent endgame liabilities.
pearls.action: Structure check before every trade.

pearls.text: Rooks behind passed pawns; don't block your own bishops. Rules are training wheels — ride them until they fall off on their own.
pearls.mechanism: Rules substitute for pattern recognition until it develops.
pearls.action: Apply Tarrasch defaults; note exceptions in review.
pearls.source: Tarrasch; Watson (on when to drop them)

pearls.text: Where your opening course ends is where your study begins.
pearls.mechanism: The resulting middlegame, not the line, decides games.
pearls.action: Study typical middlegames of your repertoire.

pearls.text: Narrow repertoire, studied as typical positions, not as lines.
pearls.mechanism: Understanding structures you reach repeatedly beats one-time tricks.
pearls.action: 3–4 openings per colour max.

pearls.text: Fix the error until it stops recurring. Don't collect errors; close them.
pearls.mechanism: Best practicers locate the exact error source and rehearse it until it stops.
pearls.action: One error type per week as study target.

pearls.text: Publish your annotations to someone stronger.
pearls.mechanism: External review finds mistakes self-review cannot.
pearls.action: Monthly review by a stronger player.

pearls.text: It's the study of the game, not the game.
pearls.mechanism: Tournament play added ΔR² = .006 over serious study.
pearls.action: Protect study time over play volume.

pearls.text: Three questions: Where are the weaknesses? Which is my worst piece? What does he want?
pearls.mechanism: Attention scaffold for positional evaluation.
pearls.action: Run on every critical position.

pearls.text: Find his best move first; then make it impossible.
pearls.mechanism: Prophylaxis: deny the opponent's most useful plan before executing your own.
pearls.action: Weekly Dvoretsky-style exercise.

pearls.text: Remove counterplay, then press.
pearls.mechanism: Opponent's need to do something generates the error.
pearls.action: Restriction before realisation.

pearls.text: The familiar pattern captures your eyes while you believe you're searching.
pearls.mechanism: Einstellung: gaze stays on the familiar idea's squares despite intent to search.
pearls.action: Force a written second candidate before committing.

pearls.text: Write the lines. Visualisation fails silently; paper doesn't.
pearls.mechanism: Written lines expose where visualisation breaks.
pearls.action: Candidate moves written in long games.

pearls.text: Mistakes are a consequence of tension. Keep the tension.
pearls.mechanism: Error rates rise with game length and complexity.
pearls.action: Play on in equal positions.

pearls.text: 'Theoretical draw' is a claim. Test it.
pearls.mechanism: Human error rates in long technical positions are high.
pearls.action: Don't agree draws in playable positions.

pearls.text: A rook outranks a knight only when it has a file.
pearls.mechanism: Nominal vs real piece value depends on open lines and blockade squares.
pearls.action: Evaluate exchange sacs by file availability.

pearls.text: Steer toward positions whose difficulty you can handle.
pearls.mechanism: Position difficulty predicts blunders (73%) better than skill (55%) or time (53%).
pearls.action: Choose structures you know over objectively 'better' unknown ones.

pearls.text: Borrow the engine's move orders and pawn-sac verdicts. Don't try to think like it.
pearls.mechanism: Engine 'ideas' beyond concrete verdicts don't transfer to human play.
pearls.action: Two-step rule: analyse without, then check.

pearls.text: Woodpecker is a commitment device, not a mechanism.
pearls.mechanism: All evidence is self-reported; repetition risks memorising positions, not patterns.
pearls.action: Optional; don't expect the repetition itself to be the active ingredient.

pearls.text: Predict, then check.
pearls.mechanism: Commitment before verification is the transferable solver-era study rule.
pearls.action: Commit to an evaluation before opening the engine.

pearls.text: Play the set position with both colours against someone stronger.
pearls.mechanism: Forces understanding of both sides' plans.
pearls.action: Dvoretsky exercise.

pearls.text: Record the novelty; let the engine sober you afterwards.
pearls.mechanism: Human-first analysis, engine-second verification.
pearls.action: Kasparov's method.

pearls.text: AlphaZero's ideas are earned, not borrowed.
pearls.mechanism: Long-term pawn sacs without understanding are dangerous.
pearls.action: H-pawn vs castled king only with a stable centre; redeploy before being kicked.

pearls.text: Fitness is hour-five stamina, not calories.
pearls.mechanism: 6,000-kcal claim is a 1975 breathing-rate extrapolation; real lever is lapses in long games.
pearls.action: Conditioning for stamina and stress.

pearls.text: Recognise more, calculate less. The 2026 Candidates was won on the clock.
pearls.mechanism: Sindarov ~25 min ahead moves 17–40; Gukesh collapsed by calculating everything.
pearls.action: Build the library; trust recognition in known structures.
pearls.source: Chess Engine Lab Candidates data; Gajewski

pearls.text: Practice buys about a third. Starting late is real. Measure error rates, not titles.
pearls.mechanism: Deliberate practice ≈34% of rating variance; starting age β=−.15 after hours.
pearls.action: Goals in metrics table, not titles.

pearls.text: No chess training method has a randomised trial behind it. Grade every piece of advice — including this document.
pearls.mechanism: All evidence is observational, retrospective or n-of-one.
pearls.action: Keep evidence grades visible in the app.

pearls.text: Don't copy a GM's childhood.
pearls.mechanism: Elite methods are tagged by the level at which they transfer; early copying is Rowson's 'inappropriate copying'.
pearls.action: Filter pearls by current stage.

metrics.name: Error-type tag
metrics.how: One of: hung_piece | missed_threat | bad_trade | wrong_plan | clock | endgame_technique

targets.all: Most frequent tag = this week's study target
Correlate with blunder metrics after 3 months

pitfalls.name: Volume substitution
pitfalls.text: Playing 10 unreviewed games instead of 2 reviewed. >90% of adult time goes to play; it is the least efficient activity.

pitfalls.name: Opening study as procrastination
pitfalls.text: Feels productive, decides nothing below 1600. Only to fix review-identified recurring problems.

pitfalls.name: Puzzle rush / themed sets
pitfalls.text: Rewards memorised puzzles; speed puzzles ≈ games in efficiency.

pitfalls.name: Eval-bar watching
pitfalls.text: Teaches what the engine thinks, not why you blundered.

pitfalls.name: Copying early
pitfalls.text: Tal/AlphaZero/Carlsen ideas before you can survive being objectively worse.

pitfalls.name: Post-shift grinding
pitfalls.text: Low encoding, high blunder rate, confidence damage.

pitfalls.name: Tool-building as avoidance
pitfalls.text: The first 8 weeks need a board, a notebook and two games a week. Build the app once you have ~20 reviewed games of your own data.

pitfalls.name: Expecting linear rating gain
pitfalls.text: Rating lags skill and follows a power law in games; judge by the metrics table.
